App.description: An application's table and its releases.

access_log.description: Which of the application's requests the access log writes, over the `[logs]` table's choice: `on`, `errors` or `off`.

access_log_exclude.description: Paths whose requests to the application the access log leaves out, besides those the `[logs]` table names.

group.description: The group, else the user's primary group.

priority.description: Which applications' scale-ups the node's budget admits first, the highest first.

slow.description: How slow one of the application's requests is to be written under `access_log = "errors"`.

umask.description: The file creation mask, in octal, for example 027.

user.description: The user the application's hosts and workers run as, when the daemon runs as root.

AppOverlay.description: What an overlay changes on an application: its maintenance mode, and its scheduled capacity, for its default worker group or `group`. Capacity does not conflict between overlays: the highest floor and ceiling stand.

answer.description: How refused methods are answered, with the values a route's `methods.answer` takes.

deny.description: Methods refused on each of the application's routes.

freeze_deploys.description: Refuse deploys and rollouts of the application unless overridden.

group.description: The worker group the capacity applies to; the default group without it.

maintenance.description: Maintenance mode while the overlay is active.

max_workers.description: The most workers, a ceiling over the group's own.

min_workers.description: The fewest workers, a floor over the group's own.

mode.description: The site mode on each of the application's routes.

scale_in.description: `hold` keeps the group from scaling in; `normal` (the default) leaves it to the autoscaler's rules.

Auth.description: A route's authentication sub-request: the edge sends a bodiless GET to an application path and serves the route only when that answers 2xx.

app.description: The application that decides; empty when an upstream does.

cache.description: Remember allowing decisions for a while (off without it).

copy_headers.description: Response headers of an allowing answer added to the request as trusted headers; a client's own copies are always removed.

path.description: The path asked, usually of an internal mount or route.

timeout.description: How long the handler has, queueing included, for example 2s.

upstream.description: The HTTP upstream that decides, instead of an application.

AuthCache.description: How long and by what an allowing decision is remembered.

key.description: What a decision is keyed by: `cookie:NAME` and `header:NAME` entries. A request with none of them present is never served from the cache.

ttl.description: How long a decision stands, for example 30s.

BorrowedThreads.description: The table form of a mount's threads.

max.description: The most requests the mount runs at once, on its reserved threads and borrowed ones together.

Budget.description: The `[daemon.budget]` table: what the releases on the node may hold between them. Each limit is off when omitted.

cpu.description: CPU cores the workers use, as measured.

memory.description: Memory for the hosts and workers, as a size such as 12GB.

workers.description: Worker processes and managed server instances.

Build.description: The `[tool.muru.build]` table: when and how the release's environment is built from the lock. `when` is read by `muructl run` and the daemon alike; the rest describes the deployment flavour, which development ignores.

groups.description: Dependency groups beyond the defaults; dev is never included.

source_builds.description: Allow sdists to be built on the node.

when.description: When an environment is built: `auto` builds a missing one and leaves an existing one alone, `always` builds on every start and on a lock change, `never` builds nothing. `muructl serve` never builds one.

oneOf.description: Build a missing environment; leave an existing one alone at start, and under `muructl run` build when the lock changes.
Build before every start too.
Build nothing.

Bytecode.description: Where compiled bytecode goes for a daemon-managed release.

oneOf.description: A writable directory of the release's own under the state directory, so nothing lands in the source tree (the default).
`__pycache__` beside the source, as Python does by default; what a release with precompiled bytecode uses.
No bytecode is written.

except.description: Files that get no-cache instead, by pattern on their path within the route.

max_age.description: How long clients may keep a file, for example 1y or 1h.

CapacitySchedule.description: An `[[app.NAME.schedule]]` entry: capacity for a window, shorthand for an overlay named `APP.NAME` that sets only the floor, the ceiling, how scale-in behaves and a deploy freeze.

freeze_deploys.description: Refuse deploys and rollouts during the window.

group.description: The worker group; the default group without it.

max_workers.description: The most workers during the window.

min_workers.description: The fewest workers during the window.

name.description: The schedule's name, unique within the application.

scale_in.description: `hold` keeps the group from scaling in during the window; `normal`, the default, leaves it to the autoscaler.

start.description: A one-off window's start, as for an overlay's schedule.

timezone.description: The time zone of local times.

warm_up.description: How long before each window the floor applies, such as 30m.

ClientClass.description: A `[[client_class]]` rule. A request gets the class when every input the rule names matches, each input matching when any of its entries does; rules are tried in order and a request that matches none is class `default`.

address_list.description: A file of addresses and networks, one a line, as for `user_agent_list`.

addresses.description: Client addresses and networks, such as 203.0.113.0/24.

cookies.description: Cookies by name, each value matched by a regular expression.

headers.description: Request headers by name, each value matched by a regular expression: a CDN's verdict, say.

ja4.description: JA4 fingerprints of the client's TLS ClientHello, or their beginnings ending in `*`.

ja4_list.description: A file of JA4 fingerprints, one a line, as for `user_agent_list`.

name.description: The class's name, as logs, metrics, rate limits and applications see it.

user_agent.description: User-Agent substrings, compared without regard to case.

user_agent_list.description: A file of User-Agent substrings, one a line, relative to the configuration file's directory and read again when it changes.

user_agent_regex.description: Regular expressions matched against the User-Agent header.

verify.description: `dns` confirms the client's address by reverse and forward lookup against `verify_domains`; until it is confirmed the rule does not match.

verify_domains.description: The domains a verified name must be, or end in.

ClientMatch.description: The requests a rate limit or route applies to.

default.description: The value when none is given.

description.description: What the value is, for `muructl command list` and prompts.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match.

required.description: The command refuses to run without it.

secret.description: The value is never shown, logged or put in an event, and may only be used in `env`.

CommandTable.description: A command an application declares, the `[tool.muru.commands.NAME]` or `[app.NAME.release.ID.commands.NAME]` table: a program to run, or a Python callable to call, with the release.

call.description: A callable as module:function, called with the inputs as keyword arguments, instead of `run`.

description.description: What the command does, for `muructl command list`.

env.description: Environment variables for this command alone, over the release's, with `{name}` where an input's value goes.

exclusive.description: Run one at a time for the application: a run asked for while one is under way is refused.

inputs.description: The values the command takes, by name.

run.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell, with `{name}` where an input's value goes; `python` is the release's interpreter.

timeout.description: How long it may run before it is stopped, for example 10m; no limit when absent.

Compression.description: The `[compression]` table: how the edge compresses responses. Every key is optional. A virtual host and a route take the same table, where a key left out is the level beneath's.

enabled.description: Whether responses are compressed at all.

encodings.description: The encodings offered in preference order: br, zstd and gzip. An empty list is refused; `enabled = false` turns compression off.

level.description: How hard to compress: fast, default or best.

min_size.description: The smallest body worth compressing, for example 1KB; at least 1 byte.

types.description: The content types compressed: exact types or a family as text/*. An empty list is refused.

Daemon.description: The `[daemon]` table of the daemon's file: how the daemon itself runs.

budget.description: The node's budget across every application.

debug_exec.description: Allow `muructl debug exec`, which runs code in a worker; off unless set.

user.description: The service user: whom a daemon that runs as root starts the edge, and the applications that name no user of their own, as. Never root.

Dashboard.description: The `[dashboard]` table: where the daemon serves its dashboard and JSON gateway, and whether it takes actions.

actions.description: Whether a person signed in with `muructl dashboard login` may act from the dashboard; read-only when false.

listen.description: The loopback address the dashboard is served on, such as 127.0.0.1:8090; not served when omitted.

EnvValue.description: A value in an `[env]` table: the text itself, or a reference to a secret in a store, delivered as the variable or, with `as = 'file'`, as a file whose path is in `NAME_FILE`.

ErrorOverride.description: Replacing an application's own error responses with error pages, the `error_override` table.

statuses.description: The statuses whose responses are replaced.

when.description: When a listed response is replaced: `all` (the default), `empty_body`, `not_json` or `html_only`.

ErrorPage.description: A custom error page: one entry of an `error_pages` table, keyed by status (`404`) or status and reason (`"503:maintenance"`). Exactly one of `file`, `template` and `path` is given.

content_type.description: The content type of a template.

file.description: A file sent as the body, with the content type its name implies. A release's page may be a path relative to its source directory; elsewhere the path is absolute.

path.description: An application path the edge asks for the page, as an internal sub-request that sees `REDIRECT_STATUS` and `muru.error_reason`.

template.description: A template the edge renders, with `{status}`, `{title}`, `{reason}`, `{description}`, `{request_id}`, `{retry_after}`, `{host}` and `{path}` filled in.

EventSink.description: An `[[events.sink]]` entry: a webhook that receives events as signed CloudEvents requests.

kind.description: The kind of sink; only webhook for now.

levels.description: Levels delivered (info, notice, warning, error); every level when empty.

secret.description: The key deliveries are signed with.

secret_file.description: A file holding the key, instead of `secret`.

types.description: Event types delivered, as patterns such as `release.*`; every type when empty.

url.description: Where deliveries go, an http:// or https:// URL.

Events.description: The `[events]` table: the sinks events are pushed to.

FactoryPhase.description: When a factory entrypoint is called.

oneOf.description: In each worker, after the post_fork hook.
Once in the host, during preload.

Fallback.description: A static route's fallback: an application, or a file within the directory.

app.description: The application that takes requests no file answers.

file.description: The file served for paths with no file of their own.

upstream.description: The HTTP upstream that takes them instead.

ForwardedHeaders.description: How forwarding headers are left after they have been applied.

oneOf.description: The configured headers stay for the application, other forwarding headers are removed.
Every forwarding header is removed; the application sees only the resolved values.

Group.description: A worker group, the `[app.NAME.release.ID.groups.NAME]` or `[tool.muru.groups.NAME]` table: the paths it serves and its own sizes. Paths not claimed by a group go to the default group, which is the release's own settings.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI worker's event loop takes at once.

match.description: What the group asks of a request beside its path: the client classes, hosts and methods it takes, each list any of its entries; a group asking more comes before one asking less, and a group with lists and no `paths` takes every path.

max_body_size.description: The largest body of a request the group serves, for example 200MB, which the edge enforces.

max_lifetime.description: How long a worker of the group lives before it is replaced, for example 1h, with jitter.

max_requests.description: Requests a worker of the group serves before it is replaced, with jitter.

memory.description: The group's own memory policy, each key the release's when absent.

mounts.description: The named mounts the group's workers serve, beside the default mount, which every worker serves; every mount when absent. The group's paths must lie within them.

optional.description: Whether the release is ready without the group's workers: its requests wait until one listens.

paths.description: Path prefixes, with an optional trailing `*`; the most specific match across all groups wins.

scaling.description: How the group is scaled; static when absent.

sync_threads.description: Threads for synchronous code called from an ASGI application.

timeouts.description: The group's own timeouts, each the release's when absent; `shutdown_timeout` and `websocket_drain_grace` belong to the release.

GroupMatch.description: The requests a worker group takes for its paths: every list given must name the request's class, host or method.

host.description: Hosts: a virtual host's name or a name it answers to, or under `muructl run` the name the request carries.

Handoff.description: The interface a release's or a mount's requests may be handed to: ASGI from a WSGI application, WSGI from an ASGI one.

oneOf.description: Continue the request as an ASGI application on the event loop.
Continue the request as a WSGI callable on the thread pool.

anyOf.description: A value for each time the header is sent.

HeaderValues.description: One value of a header, or several for a header sent more than once.

access_log.description: Which of the host's requests the access log writes: `on`, `errors` or `off`, replacing the `[logs]` table's. An application's own replaces it.

access_log_exclude.description: Paths whose requests the access log leaves out, besides those the `[logs]` table leaves out.

canonical.description: The name the host is known by, for `use_canonical_name`.

canonical_redirect.description: Redirect requests for the host's other names to the canonical name.

compression.description: How responses to the host's requests are compressed, each key replacing the daemon's `[compression]` value. A route's own replace them.

default.description: Answer requests whose host matches no virtual host, which are otherwise refused with 421.

error_override.description: Replace the application's own error responses with error pages.

error_pages.description: Custom error pages, by status or status:reason.

https_redirect.description: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS.

listeners.description: The listener addresses it answers on; every listener when empty.

maintenance.description: What the host's maintenance mode lets through, while `muructl maintenance on --host` has it on.

max_body_size.description: The largest request body for the host's routes, for example 1MB, replacing the daemon's `[limits]` value. A route's own replaces it.

names.description: The names it answers to: exact names, or `*.example.com` for one label. Compared case-insensitively, without a port or trailing dot.

rate_limits.description: The `[rate_limit.NAME]` tables applied to every request for the host, before a route's.

request_headers.description: Headers removed from, and set on, the host's requests before anything is asked to serve them. A route's own are applied after them.

response_headers.description: Headers removed from, set on and added to every response to the host's requests. A route's own are applied after them.

slow.description: How slow a request is to be written under `access_log = "errors"`.

timeouts.description: The timeouts of a request for the host's routes, each replacing the daemon's `[limits]` value. A route's own replace them.

tls.description: Its certificate and key, for TLS listeners.

use_canonical_name.description: Give the application the canonical name as SERVER_NAME rather than the name matched.

HostTls.description: A virtual host's certificate chain and private key, as PEM files.

certificate.description: The certificate chain, leaf first. A relative path is taken from the file's directory.

key.description: The private key. A relative path is taken from the file's directory.

oneOf.description: Detect from the callable: a coroutine function or an object with an `async def __call__` is ASGI, anything else WSGI.
ASGI 3.
gRPC services: the entrypoint is a registration function given a server to add grpcio servicers to.

Limits.description: The `[limits]` table: sizes and durations as the configuration writes them.

body_idle_timeout.description: Time a client may pause while sending a body.

header_read_timeout.description: Time allowed for a complete request head.

keep_alive_timeout.description: Idle time before a keep-alive connection is closed.

keep_alive_timeout_proxy.description: The same for connections from trusted proxies.

max_connections_per_client.description: Open connections per client address; 0 disables it.

max_requests_per_connection.description: Requests served on one connection before it is closed; 0 for no limit.

queue_timeout.description: Time a request may wait for a worker.

request_deadline.description: Time a request may take to produce its response head.

response_idle_timeout.description: Time a worker may pause mid-response.

spool_quota.description: What stored uploads may hold at once across every application; no limit without it.

Listener.description: A listener, one of the `[[listener]]` entries, in the daemon's own file.

h2c.description: On a listener without TLS, the clients that may speak HTTP/2 in cleartext (h2c), as addresses, ranges, loopback or private; every client when omitted, none when empty. The others are served HTTP/1.1.

limits.description: The listener's own limits on its connections and on reading a request's head, each replacing the `[limits]` value for the connections it accepts.

proxy.description: The listener's own trusted proxies and header types, in place of the whole `[proxy]` table for the connections it accepts. An empty table trusts nothing.

tls.description: Whether TLS is terminated on it, with the certificates of the virtual hosts it serves, chosen by SNI.

ListenerLimits.description: A listener's `limits` table: the keys of `[limits]` that bound a connection and the reading of a request's head, each replacing the node's for the connections the listener accepts.

header_read_timeout.description: Time allowed for a complete request head.

keep_alive_timeout.description: Idle time before a keep-alive connection is closed.

keep_alive_timeout_proxy.description: The same for connections from trusted proxies.

max_connections_per_client.description: Open connections per client address; 0 disables it.

max_requests_per_connection.description: Requests served on one connection before it is closed; 0 for no limit.

oneOf.description: Everything.
Informational messages and above.
Python's default: warnings and above.
Errors and above.
Only critical messages.

Logging.description: The `[logging]` table: how Python logging is set up in the workers.

Logs.description: The `[logs]` table of the daemon's file: how the daemon rotates the log files it and its processes write, which records the access log writes, and whether its standard streams carry the time.

access_log.description: Which requests the access log writes: `on` (the default), `errors` (4xx and 5xx responses, requests at least `slow`, and WebSockets that closed other than normally or going away) or `off`. Requests not written are still counted in the metrics and shown on the dashboard.

access_log_exclude.description: Paths whose requests the access log leaves out: `*` matches any run of characters and `?` one, for example `/static/*`.

compress.description: How archives are compressed: `zstd` (the default), `gzip` or `off`.

every.description: Rotate by the clock: `off`, `hourly`, `daily` (the default) or `weekly`, at the period's start in UTC.

size.description: Rotate a file that reaches this size, for example 100MB.

slow.description: How slow a request is to be written under `access_log = "errors"`.

timestamps.description: Put the full UTC time in front of every line the daemon writes to standard output and standard error, as `--timestamps` does, for a supervisor that stamps nothing. Files always carry the time.

Maintenance.description: What maintenance mode lets through, the `maintenance` table of a release.

bypass_cookie.description: A `name=value` cookie that lets a client through.

exempt_addresses.description: Client addresses, or ranges in CIDR form, served as usual.

exempt_paths.description: Path prefixes served as usual while the application is in maintenance.

retry_after.description: The `Retry-After` the maintenance page carries, for example 5m.

Measure.description: How a worker's memory is measured.

oneOf.description: Unique set size: pages no other process shares, the default, since preloaded pages are shared copy-on-write.
Proportional set size: shared pages counted in proportion.
Resident set size: every resident page.

Memory.description: The `[memory]` table of a release or a `[tool.muru]` table: the limits a worker's memory is held to.

hard_limit.description: Over this the worker leaves routing at once and is replaced, for example 1200MB.
hard_limit.x-default: off; under `muructl serve` with a memory limit, a share of it

measure.description: What is measured: uss (the default), pss or rss.

reclaim_first.description: Whether to collect garbage and trim the heap before recycling over the soft limit.

soft_for.description: How long the worker may stay over the soft limit.

soft_limit.description: Over this for soft_for, the worker reclaims and then recycles, for example 800MB; off when absent.

answer.description: `read_only` (the default) answers 503 read_only; `method_not_allowed` answers 405 with the methods left in Allow.

deny.description: The methods refused, for example POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.

Metrics.description: The `[metrics]` table: where the daemon serves the Prometheus exposition.

listen.description: The address `/metrics` is served on, an internal one such as 127.0.0.1:9464; not served when omitted.

Mount.description: A mount, the `[app.NAME.release.ID.mounts.NAME]` or `[tool.muru.mounts.NAME]` table: a path served by another entrypoint in the same workers. The release's own entrypoint is the default mount at /.

accel_redirect.description: Treat an `X-Accel-Redirect` response header from the mount as an internal redirect.

accept_redirects_from.description: Other applications whose internal redirects may reach the mount when it is internal; the release's own always may.

cgi_local_redirect.description: Treat a 200 response with a `Location` starting with `/` and no body as an internal redirect, the CGI convention.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI mount runs at once on each worker, slots of its own at the edge; it shares the event loop's concurrency when absent.

handoff.description: The interface the mount's requests may be handed to; none when absent.

interface.description: The interface, when declared rather than detected.

internal.description: Reachable only through internal redirects: a client's request for its path is answered 404.

max_body_size.description: The largest body of a request the mount serves, for example 200MB, which the edge enforces.
max_body_size.x-default: the worker group's, else the release's

max_connections.description: Open WebSockets an ASGI mount holds at once on each worker, apart from the requests it runs; each holds a request slot when absent.

path.description: The path prefix; the longest wins, on segment boundaries. A gRPC mount has none: its calls are matched by service name.

sendfile_header.description: A second response header honoured as `X-Muru-Sendfile` is, such as `X-Sendfile`.

sendfile_roots.description: Directories a path in an `X-Muru-Sendfile` response header must lie in for the edge to serve the file; the release's when absent, and an empty list refuses every hint.

threads.description: Threads of the mount's own, for a WSGI or gRPC mount; it shares the worker's pool when absent.

anyOf.description: A pool of this many threads, used by the mount alone.
Reserved threads, and shared ones borrowed up to a maximum.

MountThreads.description: A mount's own threads: a fixed pool, `threads = 4`, or a reserved minimum that borrows threads of the shared pool up to a maximum, `threads = { reserved = 2, max = 6 }`.

Overlay.description: An `[overlay.NAME]` table: changes to named routes and to applications, applied over the base configuration while the overlay is active, by its schedule or by hand.

advisory.description: Its schedule only raises overlay.would_activate events; it is activated by hand only.

latch.description: Once its schedule activates it, it stays active past the window until a person ends it.

preconditions.description: What must hold for the overlay to activate.

priority.description: Which of two active overlays setting the same field wins: the higher. Overlays that would conflict must both set one.

routes.description: Changes to routes, by the route's `name`.

trigger.description: When the overlay is active on its own; by hand only without it.

warm_up.description: What to start ahead of its schedule's windows.

OverlaySchedule.description: A window in time: one-off, from `start` until `end` when it has one, or recurring, from each time `cron` names for `duration`.

cron.description: When each window starts, as a cron expression such as '0 2 * * *' (see [`cron::Cron`]).

duration.description: How long each recurring window lasts, such as 1h.

end.description: When it ends; it stays active until ended or promoted without it.

start.description: When it starts, as a local date and time such as 2026-11-02T09:00, or with an offset.

timezone.description: The time zone local times are in, such as Australia/Sydney; the daemon's own zone without it.

OverlayTrigger.description: When an overlay is active on its own.

external.description: Whether the signed webhook of the `[overlay_webhook]` table may activate and end it.

OverlayWebhook.description: The `[overlay_webhook]` table: where the daemon takes signed requests from monitoring and alerting systems to activate and end the overlays that declare the external trigger.

secret.description: The key requests are signed with.

secret_file.description: A file holding the key, in place of `secret`.

Preconditions.description: What must hold for an overlay to activate.

release_ready.description: A release that must be ready, as app@release, or as release when the overlay changes routes of one application only.

Preload.description: Whether the application is imported in the host before forking.

oneOf.description: Preload when the import check passes, otherwise import per worker.
Preload, and fail the release when the import check does not pass.
Import in every worker.

Proxy.description: The `[proxy]` table: which peers are trusted to speak for the client, and through which headers.

forwarded_headers.description: What becomes of the forwarding headers once applied.

headers.description: The header types applied from trusted peers: forwarded, x-forwarded-for, x-forwarded-proto, x-forwarded-host, x-forwarded-port, x-forwarded-prefix and x-real-ip. The first four when omitted.

recursive.description: Walk a chain of addresses from the right past trusted proxies to the first untrusted one, rather than take the rightmost.

trusted.description: Addresses, CIDR ranges, or the words loopback, private and unix. Nothing is trusted when empty.

oneOf.description: Download a Python a release requests and the node lacks.
Never download; a request the node cannot satisfy fails the release.

PythonLogging.description: The `[logging.python]` table: what loggers without handlers of their own do, set before the application is imported.

capture_warnings.description: Whether warnings.warn goes through the py.warnings logger.

format.description: The format of the platform handler: standard, json, or a logging format string.

RateLimit.description: A `[rate_limit.NAME]` table: a token bucket for each key, which requests of the matching classes draw from.

action.description: `reject` (the default) answers 429, `delay` holds the request up to `max_delay` first, `log` only counts.

burst.description: How many requests a full bucket allows at once.

headers.description: Send the RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit fields with a 429.

ipv4_prefix.description: The leading bits of an IPv4 address that make the key (32).

ipv6_prefix.description: The leading bits of an IPv6 address that make the key (64).

key.description: What a bucket is kept for: `address` (the default), `client_class`, `header:NAME`, `cookie:NAME`, or a list of them.

match.description: Which requests draw from the buckets; all of them without it.

max_delay.description: The longest a request is held under `delay`.

rate.description: How fast a bucket fills, for example 2/s, 100/m or 1000/h.

Readiness.description: The `readiness` table of a managed HTTP release: how an instance is known to be ready.

path.description: The path probed with a GET until it answers 2xx or 3xx; without it, any HTTP response makes the instance ready.

timeout.description: How long the instances get to become ready.

Release.description: A release definition, the `[app.NAME.release.ID]` table: the keys a deploy takes. `muructl run --print-config` writes one so a laptop setup can become a declared release, and `muructl apply` reads them.

accel_redirect.description: Treat an `X-Accel-Redirect` response header as an internal redirect, for the default mount and any mount that does not say otherwise.

bind.description: How an `http` release's instances bind: `unix` (the default) or `port`.

build.description: When and how the environment is built on the node.

cgi_local_redirect.description: Treat a 200 response with a `Location` starting with `/` and no body as an internal redirect, the CGI convention.

command.description: The command an `http` release runs, with `{bind}` where the server takes its address; without `{bind}` the profile adds the server's own flags.

commands.description: Commands the application declares, by name: run with the release on request, with inputs.

concurrency.description: Requests an ASGI worker's event loop takes at once.

cwd.description: The directory an `http` release's command runs in; `source` when absent, and one of the two is required.

entrypoint.description: The application as module:callable, else from the source's `[tool.muru]` table.

env.description: Environment variables for the workers: a value, or a secret reference resolved when the release starts.

error_override.description: Replace the application's own error responses with error pages.

error_pages.description: Custom error pages, by status or status:reason.

factory.description: Whether the entrypoint is a factory.

grpc_web_origins.description: The origins whose pages may call the release's gRPC methods through gRPC-Web, answered with CORS: scheme, host and port, or `*`; none when empty.

handoff.description: The interface the default mount's requests may be handed to; none when absent.

hooks.description: The module holding the lifecycle hooks, as a Python module name.

instances.description: How many instances of the command an `http` release runs.

interface.description: The interface, when declared rather than detected.

kind.description: What the release runs: `workers` from an entrypoint, the default, or `http`, an HTTP server started from `command`.

logging.description: How Python logging is set up in the workers.

max_body_size.description: The largest body of a request the release serves, for example 50MB, which the edge enforces.

max_lifetime.description: How long a worker lives before it is replaced, for example 1h, with jitter; off when absent.

max_requests.description: Requests a worker serves before it is replaced, with jitter; off when absent.

memory.description: The memory policy for the workers.

preload.description: Whether the application is imported once, in the host, before the workers are forked from it.

profile.description: The server an `http` release runs: gunicorn, uvicorn, granian, mod_wsgi-express, uwsgi or generic.

python.description: The interpreter: a path, or a request in uv's syntax.

readiness.description: How an `http` release's instances are known to be ready.

reflection.description: Serve gRPC server reflection for the services the release's gRPC mounts register (default false).

scaling.description: How the default group is scaled; static when absent.

sendfile_header.description: A second response header honoured as `X-Muru-Sendfile` is, such as `X-Sendfile` for the frameworks that send that one.

sendfile_roots.description: Directories a path in an `X-Muru-Sendfile` response header must lie in for the edge to serve the file, for the default mount and any mount that does not say otherwise; with none every hint is refused.

source.description: The source directory. A relative path is taken from the file's directory. Required by `muructl apply` for a `workers` release.

static.description: The application's own static directories, served by the edge from the release's source, which is the project directory under `muructl run`.

stop_signal.description: The signal that stops an `http` release's instance gracefully: TERM, INT, QUIT, HUP, USR1, USR2 or WINCH. Required by the generic profile; the other profiles know their server's.

sync_threads.description: Threads for synchronous code called from an ASGI application.

timeouts.description: The timeouts the host enforces on its workers, and those of a request the release serves, which the edge enforces.

oneOf.description: Muru's own workers, from an entrypoint.
An HTTP server Muru starts and supervises, from a command.

RequestHeaders.description: What a virtual host or a route does to the headers of a request before anything is asked to serve it: the `request_headers` table. The names are removed first, then the headers set.

remove.description: Headers removed from the request, by name.

set.description: Headers set on the request, by name, each replacing any the client sent.

RequestTimeouts.description: The timeouts of one request, the `timeouts` table of a virtual host or a route. Each key replaces the same key of the level beneath, down to the daemon's `[limits]`.

body_idle_timeout.description: Time a client may pause while sending a body.

queue_timeout.description: Time a request may wait for a worker.

request_deadline.description: Time a request may take to produce its response head.

response_idle_timeout.description: Time a worker may pause mid-response.

ResponseHeaders.description: What a virtual host or a route does to the headers of a response: the `response_headers` table. The names are removed first, then the headers set, then those added.

add.description: Headers added to the response beside any it has, by name: a value, or a list of values for a header sent more than once.

remove.description: Headers removed from the response, by name.

set.description: Headers set on the response, by name, each replacing any the response has.

Route.description: A route, one of the `[[route]]` entries: a path prefix of a virtual host to an application.

accept_redirects_from.description: Applications other than the route's own (or a static route's fallback) whose internal redirects may reach the route. A static route with no fallback needs it for any redirect to reach it.

app.description: The application whose serving release takes the requests; empty for a static or upstream route.

auth.description: An authorisation decision the edge asks an application for before it serves the route.

cache.description: The cache headers files are sent with.

case.description: `strict` (the default), which matches names as they are on disk, or `insensitive`.

compression.description: How the route's responses are compressed, each key replacing the host's, or else the daemon's `[compression]` value.

error_override.description: Replace the application's own error responses with error pages.

error_pages.description: Custom error pages, by status or status:reason.

fallback.description: What takes a request no file answers.

hash.description: The digests computed while receiving: sha256 (the default), sha384, sha512 or sha1; an empty list for none.

index.description: The files tried, in order, when a directory is requested.

internal.description: Reachable only through internal redirects: a client's request for the path is answered 404.

match.description: The client classes the route takes; every request without it. Among routes with the same path, one naming the request's class comes first.

max_body_size.description: The largest request body, for example 1GB, replacing the host's, or else the daemon's `[limits]` value, for the route. On an upload route it bounds the body as received, files included.

max_file_size.description: The largest uploaded file, for example 512MB; no limit without it.

max_files.description: The most files in one request.

mode.description: The site mode passed to the application as muru.mode, for example read-only.

name.description: A name for the route, unique among routes, by which overlays change it.

path.description: The path prefix, `/` for everything. The longest prefix wins.

precheck.description: Ask the application with the request's headers alone first, and read the body only when it answers 2xx.

rate_limits.description: The `[rate_limit.NAME]` tables applied to the route's requests, after the host's.

redirect_slash.description: Whether a directory asked for without a trailing slash is redirected to the slash form.

request_headers.description: Headers removed from, and set on, the route's requests before anything is asked to serve them, after the host's.

response_headers.description: Headers removed from, set on and added to every response to the route's requests, after the host's.

spool_quota.description: What the application's stored uploads may hold at once when a request on the route arrives.

static.description: The directory served by the edge, instead of an application.

timeouts.description: The timeouts of the route's requests, each replacing the host's, or else the daemon's `[limits]` value.

traffic.description: How requests are shared between the application's releases; without it every request goes to the serving release.

upload.description: `multipart` or `raw` makes the edge receive and store uploads before the application sees the request; off without it.

upstream.description: The HTTP upstream that takes the requests, instead of an application.

RouteOverlay.description: What an overlay changes on a route.

answer.description: How refused methods are answered, with the values a route's `methods.answer` takes.

client_routes.description: Routes for client classes at the route's host and path, by class: each a copy of the route with these changes, or the route for that class already there with them.

error_pages.description: Error pages, by status or status:reason, each in place of the route's page for the same key.

rate_limits.description: The rate limits, in place of the route's.

request_headers.description: The headers removed from and set on the route's requests, in place of the route's `request_headers`.

response_headers.description: The headers removed from, set on and added to the route's responses, in place of the route's `response_headers`.

traffic.description: The traffic policy: a pin sends every request to one release.

RouteTarget.description: What serves a route under an overlay: one of an application, a static directory or an upstream.

Scaling.description: The `scaling` table of a release, a worker group or a `[tool.muru]` table: the mode, the bounds, and the windows and budgets that keep the autoscaler from churning. The release's own table is the default group's.

churn_budget.description: Reaps allowed per hour per release before scale-in is suspended.

hold_after_growth.description: No scale-in this long after a scale-out.

host_idle_timeout.description: How long the release's host stays once every group has scaled to zero, after which it stops too and the next request starts it again; it stays while the release runs when omitted. In the release's own scaling table.

idle_reap_after.description: A group wholly idle this long scales in without waiting for the scale-in window.

max_spare.description: Spare mode: scale in while more idle workers than this remain.
max_spare.x-default: the larger of 3 and a quarter of `max_workers`

max_step_up.description: The most workers one scale-out adds.

max_workers.description: The most workers; required by the spare and target modes.

min_lifetime.description: No worker younger than this is reaped.
min_lifetime.x-default: the larger of 15m and 30 times the time to ready

min_spare.description: Spare mode: scale out when fewer idle workers than this remain.

queue_wait_p95.description: Target mode: scale out while the p95 queue wait is over this, for example 100ms; off when absent.

reap_interval.description: At most one worker reaped per this interval.

scale_in_window.description: How long every scale-in condition must hold.

scale_out_window.description: How long a scale-out condition must hold.

slot_utilization.description: Target mode: the share of slots to keep busy, between 0 and 1.

ScalingMode.description: How a worker group is scaled.

oneOf.description: A fixed worker count, the default.
Keep between min_spare and max_spare idle workers, Apache-style.
Track a slot utilization and a queue wait target.

SecretRef.description: Which secret: a store declared in the daemon's file, and a key in it.

command.description: For an exec store, the command and arguments, with `{key}` where the key goes.

path.description: For a file store, the directory; the daemon's secrets directory under the store's name otherwise.

timeout.description: For an exec store, how long the command may take.

SecretValue.description: A secret reference in an `[env]` table.

as.description: How the value is delivered: `env` as the variable, or `file` as a file only the release's user can read, whose path is in `NAME_FILE`.

Secrets.description: The `[secrets]` table of the daemon's file.

ServerBind.description: How a managed HTTP release's instances bind.

oneOf.description: A Unix socket per instance under the release's run directory.
A free loopback port per instance.

ServerProfile.description: The server a managed HTTP release runs, which fixes how it binds and how it is stopped.

oneOf.description: gunicorn: `--bind unix:PATH` or `--bind HOST:PORT`, stopped by TERM.
uvicorn: `--uds PATH` or `--host HOST --port PORT`, stopped by TERM.
Granian: `--uds PATH` or `--host HOST --port PORT`, stopped by TERM.
mod_wsgi-express: `--host HOST --port PORT`, stopped by TERM.
uWSGI: `--http-socket PATH` or `--http-socket HOST:PORT`, with `--master` and a hook that makes TERM a graceful stop, which in uWSGI 2.0 would otherwise reload.
Any server: the command binds through `{bind}` and `stop_signal` says how it is stopped.

Shutdown.description: The `[shutdown]` table of the daemon's file: what SIGTERM and SIGINT mean to the daemon, and how a shutdown runs.

budget.description: How long the whole shutdown may take, the delay, the drain, the workers and the edge together; what has not finished by then is killed.

delay.description: How long the edge keeps accepting after the signal, closing each connection after its response so clients reconnect elsewhere, for example 5s.

on_sigterm.description: `shutdown`, which drains and stops every release and the edge before the daemon exits, or `detach`, which leaves them serving for the next daemon; shutdown when the daemon is a container's main process, detach otherwise.
on_sigterm.x-default: `shutdown` as a container's main process, else `detach`

SinkKind.description: The kind of an event sink.

StaticDir.description: A directory of an application's own files, an entry of the `[[tool.muru.static]]` or `[[app.NAME.release.ID.static]]` array: a path prefix the edge serves from a directory under the release's source, with the application taking what no file answers. Served by `muructl run` and the daemon alike, from the release the request was routed to.

cache.description: The cache headers files are sent with.

case.description: `strict` (the default), which matches names as they are on disk, or `insensitive`.

dir.description: The directory, relative to the source directory, or absolute.

fallback.description: The file served for paths with no file of their own, for a single-page application under the prefix.

index.description: The files tried, in order, when a directory is requested.

path.description: The path prefix, such as `/static/`; the longest wins, on segment boundaries, and `/` is not allowed, since every path would then be looked up as a file first.

redirect_slash.description: Whether a directory asked for without a trailing slash is redirected to the slash form.

Timeouts.description: The `[timeouts]` table of a release or a `[tool.muru]` table: the timeouts the host enforces on its workers, and the four the edge enforces on a request the release serves, which are otherwise the virtual host's or the daemon's `[limits]`.

body_idle_timeout.description: Time a client may pause while sending a body to what is served here.

gil_stall_timeout.description: How long a worker may go with no thread running Python, or with no report to its host, before it is replaced as for the hard timeout.

hard_drain_grace.description: How long a worker being replaced is given to finish its other requests before it is told to stop.

hard_timeout.description: How long a request may run in a worker before the worker is replaced, for example 60s; off when absent. Must exceed the soft timeout by at least 5s.

loop_stall_timeout.description: How long an ASGI worker's event loop may go without running before the worker is replaced as for the hard timeout.

queue_timeout.description: Time a request served here may wait for a worker, which the edge enforces; the virtual host's when absent, or else the daemon's `[limits]` value.

request_deadline.description: Time a request served here may take to produce its response head.

response_idle_timeout.description: Time a worker here may pause mid-response.

shutdown_timeout.description: How long a worker told to stop is given before it is killed, counted from when its WebSockets are closed.

soft_timeout.description: How long a request may run in a worker before it is interrupted by raising `muru.RequestTimeout` in its thread, for example 30s; off when absent.

websocket_drain_grace.description: How long a worker told to stop keeps its open WebSockets before it closes them with 1001.

Tools.description: The `[tools]` table of the daemon's file: uv, and how interpreters are installed.

offline.description: No network at all: nothing is downloaded, so a build installs only what the daemon's uv cache already holds.

python_downloads.description: Whether a Python the node lacks is downloaded for a release that requests it.

python_install_dir.description: Where managed interpreters go; a shared read-only directory for several daemons.

uv.description: The uv to run, in place of the lookup order (`MURU_UV`, a uv beside muructl, uv on PATH, the managed copy).

uv_config.description: A `uv.toml` passed to builds as their configuration file, for mirrors and TLS settings; the project's own `[tool.uv]` still applies.

uv_version.description: The uv versions accepted, as a specifier such as `>=0.9`; the daemon reports what an older one cannot do.

wheel_dir.description: A local directory of wheels for the runtime library.

Traffic.description: A route's traffic policy: the share of requests each release takes, the key requests are bucketed by, and stickiness.

classes.description: The release, by id, or `upstream:NAME`, that takes every request of a client class, ahead of stickiness and the split.

hash_key.description: What a request is bucketed by: `cookie` (the default, an anonymous id cookie the edge issues), `header:NAME`, `cookie:NAME`, or `client` (the client address). A missing header or cookie falls back to the client address.

salt.description: Mixed into the hash, so two routes split the same users differently.

split.description: Percent of requests to each release, by id; the application's serving release takes the rest. A release at 0 is reached only by preview or by a sticky cookie.

sticky.description: Whether a client keeps the release it first got, through a cookie.

sticky_grace.description: How long sticky clients keep a release that is leaving the route alive, for example 10m.

TrafficOverlay.description: An overlay's traffic policy for a route.

pin.description: Send every request to this release of the route's application.

split.description: Shares by release, in place of the route's split.

Upstream.description: An HTTP upstream, one of the `[upstream.NAME]` tables: an unmanaged HTTP server that routes, fallbacks, traffic shares and authentication sub-requests can target.

addresses.description: Where the server listens: `host:port` entries, or `unix:/path` for a Unix socket. Requests take the addresses in turn, and one that fails is set aside for a while.

connect_timeout.description: How long a connection may take to open, for example 5s.

health.description: Active health checks and passive ejection.

protocol.description: `http1` (the default), `h2c` (HTTP/2 in the clear, by prior knowledge) or `h2` (HTTP/2 over TLS).

sendfile_header.description: A second response header honoured as `X-Muru-Sendfile` is, such as `X-Sendfile`.

sendfile_roots.description: Directories a path in a trusted `X-Muru-Sendfile` response header must lie in for the edge to serve the file; with none every hint is refused.

trust_muru_headers.description: Honour X-Muru-Redirect from the upstream, as from an application: its X-Muru-* response headers are otherwise removed.

UpstreamHealth.description: An upstream's health checks: probes of each address, and the ejection of one whose requests fail.

eject_after.description: Failed requests in a row before an address is ejected; 0 never ejects.

eject_for.description: How long an ejected address is left out before a request tries it again, for example 30s; doubled each time the trial fails, up to ten times as long.

healthy_after.description: Successful probes in a row before it is healthy again.

interval.description: How often each address is probed, for example 10s.

path.description: The path probed with a GET, healthy on 2xx or 3xx; without it a connection that opens is healthy.

timeout.description: How long a probe may take, for example 2s.

unhealthy_after.description: Failed probes in a row before an address is unhealthy.

UpstreamTls.description: How an upstream's TLS connections are made.

ca.description: A PEM file of the certificates trusted, by absolute path; the public roots without it.

server_name.description: The name the certificate must carry, sent as SNI; the address's host without it.

WarmUp.description: An overlay's warm-up: for `lead` before each window of its schedule, `start_release` runs, so a switch to it lands on warm workers.

lead.description: How long before the window, such as 30m.

start_release.description: The release to start, as app@release, or as release when the overlay changes routes of one application only.

description: A declarative configuration file as `muructl apply` reads it and `muructl config export` writes it: listeners and limits, which belong to the daemon's own file, and applications with their releases.

client_class.description: Client classification rules, in order, from the daemon's own file.

error_override.description: Replace the application's own error responses with error pages.

error_pages.description: Custom error pages, by status or status:reason.

logs.description: Log rotation and the access log.

overlay.description: Overlays by name: partial configuration laid over the routes and applications while active.

proxy.description: Trusted proxies and the headers taken from them.

rate_limit.description: Rate limits by name, from the daemon's own file.

shutdown.description: What SIGTERM means to the daemon, and how a shutdown runs.

title: The daemon's configuration and applied files
